facts.statement: The study analyzed records from 38 children and teenagers, aged 3 to 18, who had been formally diagnosed with cyclic vomiting syndrome at a Wisconsin hospital.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Participants and their caregivers filled out questionnaires about symptoms during vomiting episodes and a specific tool used to measure how much the condition interferes with daily life.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Researchers used statistical methods to check how well seven different combined scores of episode details matched the measured level of disability.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: For both the general group and the migraine-associated subgroup, the combined scores were more closely linked to disability than any single symptom measure on its own.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: In the main group, the scores that combined episode frequency, duration, and nausea severity had the strongest link to the level of disability.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: In the subgroup with migraine-associated symptoms, the score combining frequency, duration, and headache pain was most strongly associated with disability.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors describe the results as a preliminary step toward validating a scale that measures the burden of the condition in children.
facts.subject: humans
